dedupe_keys.name: armas aviation radiation measurements ml ready effective dose rate datasets and radiation data portal

description: These datasets pair 92,476 in-flight effective dose rate measurements from 589 aircraft flights with the space weather conditions at the time, ready for machine learning that nowcasts radiation at aviation altitudes. The ARMAS experiment of Space Environment Technologies made the measurements from 2013 to 2023, and Georgia State University's DMLab, with NASA Ames and Langley researchers, added NAIRAS model nowcasts, GOES X-ray and proton fluxes, OMNIWeb solar wind, neutron monitor counts, geomagnetic indices and sunspot number, then split flights into training, validation and test partitions. Coverage is worldwide flight routes. Format and access: three versions (static, 1-hour and 24-hour histories) on the Radiation Data Portal, with per-flight files in the ARMAS archive. Licence: not stated on the pages read, and free to download. Caveats: measurements come from one instrument family on a limited set of flights, and the test accuracy is only slightly better than physics models. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies of space weather effects on aircrew, passengers and avionics. Related catalogue records are the BoM World Data Centre for Space Weather and the Aalto-1 RADMON radiation monitor.
